newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Don't ignore us on NATO, Russian minister warns.
newsitem.headline: Don't ignore us on NATO, Russian minister warns.

text.p: Any expansion of NATO membership without taking Russian concerns into account could lead to "serious changes" in Moscow's foreign policy, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Friday.
"Under these conditions we would be forced to think of very serious changes, including in the conduct of foreign relations," Yevgeny Primakov told journalists.

Primakov, speaking after addressing parliament behind closed doors, did not elaborate on what policy changes he had in mind. He was outlining one of three possible outcomes of the West's determination to issue invitations to former Warsaw Pact members.
The first option was that NATO would decide against accepting new members but Primakov said that this scenario "was not likely".
The second possibility, he said, was a serious effort by NATO members to consider Russia's concerns on the alliance's expansion -- which Russian officials say could threaten Moscow's security.
"It is to this end that we are striving," he said. "It is precisely because of this that we have started consultations and negotiations with NATO," he said.
